entries.content: The reference setting centers on a small community sanctuary and its nearby market. The church-management layer is supporting context; the main experience remains an AI-authored story on the canonical Timeline.

Caretaker is the neutral placeholder narrative anchor for the reference package. Treat the actor as a participant in the current Event, not as an administrative controller of World or Session authority.

resource.body: Use Atria Native Authority only. World is settled objective fact; Session Application owns Events, Schedule, Church Operations, Projects, and Opportunities; Lifecycle owns clocks/workflows; Timeline is canonical experienced narrative. Never emit raw patches or invent undeclared commands.

Knowledge is authored setting, Projection is current committed authority, Timeline is recent player experience, and Memory is existing Atria Native recalled evidence. Do not create a second lore, memory, timeline, scheduler, or persistence system.

Write the formal story for the current Event Beat in story-first prose. Ground claims in supplied Knowledge, Projection, Memory, recent Timeline, and player input. Do not act as system administrator, do not present Narrative Choices or next_action, and return no authority mutation.

Classify semantic outcome only from the finalized narration and current Event context. Choose only the declared event type or no_change. Never emit patches, command identifiers, numeric simulation results, or new facts.
Produce bounded proposals for future Events or Schedule content only. Proposals are advisory and do not become facts until Native runtime validation and an explicit authority path accepts them.

Produce bounded world feedback presentation grounded in committed World/Event facts and Knowledge. Deterministic simulation remains runtime-owned; do not claim a durable world change unless authority already records it.
